summary: Requirements gate for cache-bug: one cold read (task-mttuwfzc-iz11oe) of the confirmed spec against repo reality returned seven implementation-shaping gaps, all repository-answered; the confirmed spec is left as recorded (its spec-gate read cap is exhausted) and every resolution is carried verbatim into the plan as binding requirements R1-R7; frontier closed by the human in one ledgered round.
gaps: Generation fence written as plain equality; reset_at is nullable so a never-reset session would match no row
Partial usage on errored turns unspecified: adapters could double-write, omit the mark, or invent a second event shape
DeepAgents usage does not carry the resolved route (fallback over-counts); cache writes called n/a though OpenAI and OpenRouter report nonzero cache_write_tokens
/new reset returns void and deletes rows; no way for references to leave the transaction or for cleanup failure to be emitted
Runner-output forwarder carries no sessionId and persists payloads unredacted; a raw cleanup error could leak a provider-session handle
Lost retirement race re-read would hydrate memory again, violating decision 0078 exactly-once
runtime-components.md and a second architecture page say cold runs are memory-only, contradicting session-resume.md and the intended retirement path
contradictions: 0078 exactly-once hydration vs a default re-read on a lost race
session-resume.md stored-handle resume vs architecture pages saying cold runs are memory-only
resolutions: Gap 1 — null-safe IS NOT DISTINCT FROM on every generation fence, with null/null success and null/non-null rejection tests (plan requirement R1; carried as spec amendment text in the plan input)
Gap 2 — final error output carries one cumulative partial-usage payload with the stable usage identifier; host records the mark exactly once (plan R2)

Gap 3 — every executable route declares explicit read/write inclusion booleans, registry validator rejects missing ones, DeepAgents normaliser carries the resolved route; OpenAI/OpenRouter nonzero write-token tests (plan R3)
Gap 4 — /new reset returns immutable retired references after commit; handler replies then dispatches best-effort cleanup; process-loss orphans covered by the operator scan (plan R4)

Gap 5 — host publishes both new events directly through the runtime event exchange (0013) with sessionId; cleanup error sanitised, never an external session id; publish/query/projection proof (plan R5)
Gap 6 — lost-race re-read uses hydrateMemory:false and the existing generation-fenced carry from the compaction-delta path (plan R6)
Gap 7 — align runtime-components.md and the second page with session-resume.md as a canon edit inside the task (plan R7)
Contradiction 1 — resolved for 0078 via the fenced carry pattern (plan R6)
Contradiction 2 — resolved for session-resume.md via the docs alignment (plan R7)

rounds.question: Requirements gate closing question. The single cold read found seven implementation-shaping gaps (null-safe generation fence, one cumulative partial-usage payload on errors, explicit cache read/write booleans per route with the resolved route carried, /new returning retired references after commit, host-published events with a sanitised error, non-hydrating lost-race re-read per 0078, and aligning two architecture pages with session-resume.md). All seven are answered by the repository. Because the confirmed spec cannot be re-saved without a fresh spec-gate read and that gate's read cap is used up, they become binding plan requirements R1 to R7 rather than spec edits. Any remaining gap before I record the requirements gate and author the plan?
options: No remaining gap, record and plan (Recommended)
